These batteries use nickel oxide hydroxide and metallic cadmium as their positive and negative electrodes, respectively. This size makes it compatible with a wide range of devices, including remote controls, digital cameras, portable radios, and more. Capacity: The battery has a capacity of 1000mAh (milliampere-hours). This voltage is typical for rechargeable Ni-Cd batteries. It's lower than the 1.5 volts of non-rechargeable alkaline batteries, so some devices may not operate at their full potential with Ni-Cd batteries. However, it's compatible with most devices designed for AA batteries. Rechargeable: One of the primary advantages of this battery is that it is rechargeable. This means you can use it multiple times by recharging it when it runs out of power, which can save money and reduce waste compared to single-use disposable batteries. Charging: Ni-Cd batteries require a specific charger designed for Ni-Cd chemistry. Overcharging or improper charging can reduce their lifespan or even cause damage, so it's important to use a compatible charger. Memory Effect: Ni-Cd batteries are known for their susceptibility to a phenomenon called "memory effect." This means that if you don't fully discharge the battery before recharging it, it may "remember" the reduced capacity, resulting in shorter runtimes. To mitigate this, it's recommended to perform occasional deep discharges and charges. Environmental Considerations: Cadmium, one of the components in Ni-Cd batteries, is a heavy metal and poses environmental concerns. Because of this, many countries have restricted the use of Ni-Cd batteries and encourage the use of more environmentally friendly alternatives like nickel-metal hydride (Ni-MH) or lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries.

It is also sometimes referred to as a DE-9 connector. Gender: The connector is "female," which means it has receptacles (holes) to accept male connectors with exposed pins. Right Angle Design: The key feature of this connector is its right-angle design, where the cable entry or the back of the connector is at a 90-degree angle to the connector's face. This design is beneficial when there is limited space, and it allows for neater cable routing and reduces strain on the cable and connector. Pin Configuration: The DB9 connector has 9 pins, and each pin serves a specific purpose in data communication or other applications. The pinout typically includes pins for transmitting and receiving data, ground connections, and other control signals depending on the specific application. Application: DB9 connectors were commonly used in serial communication interfaces, such as RS-232, for connecting devices like computer serial ports, modems, printers, and other peripherals. However, with the advancement of technology, they are becoming less common in modern devices, often replaced by more compact and advanced connectors like USB and HDMI. Screw Locks: Some DB9 connectors may have screws on either side of the connector's face, allowing for a more secure connection when mated with the appropriate screws on the male connector.

fullDesc: The NFC IC 125kHz bracelet RFID is a type of wearable device that utilizes Near Field Communication (NFC) technology and operates at a frequency of 125kHz. It is commonly used for identification and access control applications in various industries, such as access management, security, attendance tracking, and payment systems. NFC (Near Field Communication) Technology: NFC is a short-range wireless communication technology that enables data transfer between devices when they are in close proximity (usually within a few centimeters). It allows for quick and easy interactions between the bracelet and NFC-enabled devices, such as smartphones, access control readers, or payment terminals. IC (Integrated Circuit): The NFC IC within the bracelet is a microchip that stores and processes data. It contains an antenna for communication with external devices and is responsible for handling the RFID functions of the bracelet. RFID (Radio Frequency Identification): The bracelet incorporates RFID technology, which allows it to wirelessly exchange data with compatible RFID readers. The RFID system typically consists of a reader and one or more RFID tags (in this case, the bracelet acts as the RFID tag). fullDesc: An SD (Secure Digital) memory card slot is a common feature found in many electronic devices, including digital cameras, smartphones, tablets, laptops, and other portable devices. The slot is designed to accommodate SD memory cards, which are small, removable storage devices. SD memory cards come in various sizes, including standard SD, miniSD, and microSD. The slot is typically designed to accept one or more of these card sizes, depending on the device. The cards themselves are rectangular in shape and have a contact area with metal connectors on one side. These connectors establish a connection between the memory card and the device it's inserted into. The SD card slot is usually located on the side or front of the device and may have a cover or a protective flap to keep out dust and debris when not in use. To use the slot, you insert the SD memory card into the appropriate slot with the contact side facing down. Pushing the card gently until it clicks into place ensures proper insertion. SD memory cards provide a means of expanding the storage capacity of a device, allowing users to store more files, photos, videos, and other data. They are commonly used for storing and transferring media files, such as photos and videos, but they can also be used to store other types of data, including documents, music, and applications. It's important to note that SD memory cards have different capacities, ranging from a few gigabytes (GB) to multiple terabytes (TB), with the capacity labeled on the card itself. The read and write speeds of SD cards can also vary, depending on the card's class or speed rating. These ratings indicate how quickly data can be read from or written to the card. Overall, an SD memory card slot provides a convenient and portable way to expand the storage capabilities of devices, allowing users to easily transfer and access their data across multiple devices.

The Ai-Thinker company in Shenzen has recently introduced two new LoRa radio modules, the Ra-08 and Ra-08H. These new LoRaWAN modules are based on the ASR Microelectronics ASR6601 module featuring a 48MHz ARM Cortex M4 microcontroller and Semtech SX1262 transceiver allowing long-range, low power communication for the Internet of Things. Both LoRaWAN modules share most of the same specifications, but the Ra-08 module operates in the 410-525MHz frequency band, while the Ra-08H module works in the widely used 803MHz to 930MHz band. This means that it can connect to WiFi networks that are further away or have weaker signals. Smaller size: The ESP-12F is slightly smaller than the ESP-12E. fullDesc: STM32 Bluepill based upon stm32F103C8T6 is a very poular and economical board used by students, hobbyists and application development engineers. The board however needs external devices like buttons, kcd, status leds etc for testing. These are usually made on breadboard and work great. The down side is that this breadboard setup has to be done everytime you start a new project, and the connections are wuite unstable sometimes. Bluebird is the Nikrotronics pakistan and hallroad.org joint product where a standard playground fas been provided for the Bluepill boared. The devices commonly used in projects are provided on board along with their power supply and open headers for interfacing connections. The connections then can be made to any IO lines of bluepill using female jumper wires (that are very stable). any other module, like motor driver etc that is not fabricated on board can be easily interfaced using jumper wires. Features: Hosting socket for STM32F103C8 Bluepill board All IO lines available as headers for easy jumper connections Clear labelling of all pins with Arduino pin numbers, PORT Pin Names and alternate functions. Onboard external DC Power supply 9-12V and on board 5V and 3,3V 1A regulators 5V and 3.3V Supply available through a header for external modules. HD44780 Character LCD Socket (Spports all 16×2, 16×4, 20×4 LCD) in 4 bit mode ST7735 based Full colour TFT SPI Display Support 8 Staus LEDs (Red, Green, Blue and White) 1 RGB LED 1 POT 0-3.3V for analog testing Two Push Buttons with active Low configuration Header for direct connection of FT232 module to USART1 for serial communication and loading programs using internal Bootloader Header for ST-Link Programmer and Debugger. With two pins to be connected to Bluepill SWDIO and SWCLK pins. ST7735 TFT Display Be noted that ST7735 TFT modules come in various connection footprints. This board Has connections in this order as shown in Image below. If you have a different TFT display you can use direct jumper wire connections to use it. ST-Link Programmer and Debugger The header provided for ST-Link V2 is as per standard Pinouts of the device. However some Chinese manufacturers have a device with different Pinouts so check your ST-Link pinouts before using on this connector. In case of different pinouts you can connect ST-Link Directly to the Bluepill header using jumper wires.
